metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets Costa Rica

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results for Costa Rica using the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment administered to 15-year-olds across participating countries and economies. The factsheet does not provide the underlying microdata weighting variables (e.g., student/sampling weights or replicate weights) or the exact analytic filtering steps used to compute the reported means, proficiency shares, correlations, and relative success indicators. For users working with PISA microdata, analysts should apply the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights (if available in the dataset) to obtain correct standard errors under the complex survey design. Because this is a published results factsheet rather than a re-estimation study, the manuscript does not specify whether weights were applied in the computations shown; therefore, weight-aware replication should follow the PISA technical documentation and the OECD/IEA database guidance.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because the document is a results factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 creative thinking outcomes rather than reporting an original student-level predictive model with explicit PV estimation procedures. The factsheet also does not describe a missing-data strategy (e.g., PV-based multiple imputation or case deletion rules) because it is not an analysis methods paper; it reports OECD-produced estimates from the PISA database. As a result, the PV and missing-data handling details are not transparently documented at the factsheet level.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports Costa Rica results for the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test implemented in 64 countries/economies. For Costa Rica, 6,113 students in 198 schools completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 57,200 15-year-olds (estimated 78% of the total 15-year-old population). No additional student-level inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., missingness rules, specific task completion filters) are provided in the factsheet; it presents the OECD’s published estimates for the Costa Rica analytic population.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes creative thinking performance for Costa Rica among 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Costa Rica’s mean creative thinking score is 27 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average of 33. About 64% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline proficiency), and 11% are top performers at Levels 5–6. The factsheet also reports relative strengths (higher proficiency in evaluating/improving ideas, and in visual expression and social problem solving) and subgroup patterns (girls outperform boys by 1 score point; the gender gap is smaller than the OECD average). It further notes COVID-19-related implementation disruptions and provides caution flags for some countries/economies, but it does not provide microdata methods such as PV estimation or missing-data handling at the factsheet level.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a published OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. It does not report an original predictive modeling pipeline, target variables, model metrics, or algorithmic methods; therefore, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty. The factsheet also does not provide PV estimation or missing-data handling procedures because it reports already-produced OECD estimates from the PISA database.
